answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Book ISBN registration with publisher catalogue entry. It demands a book registered under one publisher catalogue entry, and the vault is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a book registered under one publisher catalogue entry — so privacy survives, and the sonnet is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The ripple is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
